source_spans.locator: Psychological Review 89(4), published pp.369-370, Abstract and opening framework: fact-mediated interpretation precedes direct procedure-based performance; practice drives gradual conversion, followed by continued tuning and speedup

Psychological Review 89(4), published pp.382-384, compilation protocols and mechanisms: speedup, loss of verbal rehearsal, unitary application; composition combines sequential operations, whereas proceduralization embeds retrieved factual products into new procedures and reduces working-memory demand

Psychological Review 89(4), published p.389, comparison of compilation mechanisms: composition can encode sequences while remaining general, whereas proceduralization produces more task-specific procedures; conversion preserves the behavior licensed by prior interpretation

Psychological Review 89(4), published pp.391-392, generalization section: comparison of multiple learned procedures extracts common structure and broadens application beyond the initial specific cases

Psychological Review 89(4), published pp.392-395, discrimination and strengthening sections: discrimination restricts overly broad application using correct/incorrect cases and feedback; strength adjustments alter selection and successful application of competing procedures

Psychological Review 89(4), published pp.398-400, skill-speedup analysis: algorithmic changes reduce the expected number of applied operations, strengthening reduces time per operation, and under stated assumptions practice produces an approximate power-function decrease in processing time

Psychological Review 89(4), published pp.403-404, Summary and conclusion: the progression from fact-mediated interpretation to compiled direct performance and continual tuning is explicitly described as an approximate stage analysis; different components of one task may occupy different points in the progression simultaneously

conditions: source-theory account of acquiring and practicing symbolic or rule-governed task performance
repeated task experience can transform the structures used to generate performance
substrate: fact-encoded information and executable condition-action structures in the source model
task: symbolic and problem-solving tasks, with detailed evidence from geometry-proof acquisition and supporting evidence from automatization, language, and category-learning domains
temporal_scope: initial fact-mediated performance, followed by gradual conversion to more direct executable procedures, followed by continued tuning and speedup
different components of one task may occupy different points in this progression at the same time

nodes.description: domain instructions and problem information represented as facts that must initially be interpreted to guide behavior
pre-existing general procedures that operate on fact-encoded information to generate early task behavior
task behavior generated by interpreting fact-encoded information with general procedures
a sequence of executable operations used while solving a task
learning process that combines successively applied operations into a single operation with the effect of the sequence
single executable structure that embodies a previously sequential set of operations and can reduce the number of applications needed for a task
learning process that embeds the useful products of factual retrieval into executable structures so the factual information need not be retrieved and maintained during each application
direct executable structure specialized enough to perform a practiced task without the same fact-retrieval requirements as early interpreted performance
amount of task-relevant information that must be retrieved and kept active during execution
learning process that compares multiple learned structures, extracts common structure, and broadens their range of appropriate application
learning process that uses correct and incorrect applications and feedback to restrict structures that apply too broadly
learning process that changes the relative strength of executable structures as a function of successful application and feedback
repeated opportunities to perform and receive consequences from the task
time required to execute the practiced task or its component operations

relations.description: early performance is generated by general procedures interpreting fact-encoded task information
successively used operations can be combined into a single executable structure that preserves the effect of the sequence while reducing the number of separate applications
repeated use can create a task-bound executable structure in which products formerly obtained by retrieving factual information are embedded directly
embedding formerly retrieved factual products reduces the need to retrieve and maintain that information during execution
formation of a direct executable structure does not require loss of the corresponding fact-encoded information; both may remain available
comparison across learned structures can broaden appropriate applicability by retaining common structure and dropping unnecessary specificity
experience with correct and incorrect applications can narrow overly broad applicability by adding discriminating conditions or actions
successful application and feedback alter relative strength, affecting which competing executable structures are selected and how efficiently they apply

practice-related speedup is attributed to both reductions in the expected number of operations and faster application of individual operations; under the source model's stated assumptions the resulting decrease in processing time is approximately power-shaped

the source proposes a typical component-level progression from fact-mediated performance toward direct executable performance, while explicitly treating the stage description as an approximation rather than an exclusive whole-task partition
